summary: SPHEREx Sky Shift Visualizer is a web tool that shows how objects in the sky appear to move between NASA SPHEREx survey epochs. SPHEREx maps the whole sky every six months in 102 infrared bands, and most moving objects are hard to spot by hand. Our tool lets users select a target, such as the fast-moving brown dwarf WISE 0855-0714, and blink through epochs so its motion stands out. This makes moving-object discovery easier for anyone, not just specialists. The current version is a prototype with simulated positions. The next step is loading real SPHEREx cutouts for the test targets.
details: SPHEREx Sky Shift Visualizer is a web prototype that lets a user pick a target and watch it move across SPHEREx's six-monthly sky maps, using a slider or an auto-blink to step through the epochs. The tool is a single web page built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, and it draws each target on a canvas, shifting its position for each epoch according to its proper motion. It is designed to make moving-object discovery easier for anyone, not only specialists, by providing a simple visual comparison that lowers the barrier for volunteers and students. The team chose a time-lapse style display with a blink comparator and a simple target-selection interface rather than a static image viewer, and considered ease of use for non-experts, clear labelling of simulated data, and a design that can later connect to real SPHEREx cutouts without a full rewrite. Proper motion values for WISE 0855-0714 and Barnard's Star come from published literature, while the values for Epsilon Indi B and RW Aurigae are not verified. This version is a prototype with simulated positions and no NASA data loaded yet, and loading real SPHEREx cutouts is the next step.
